recipe.visualDefinition: A vertical split-screen composition featuring a high-contrast studio portrait on the left and a structured typographic tracklist on the right, separated by a hard vertical edge. The left side uses a dark, moody background to emphasize a central figure and a vintage microphone, while the right side uses a light, off-white background with horizontal rules to organize text.
coreVisualRelationships: The vertical split divides the frame into exactly two halves: image and information.
The vintage microphone acts as a secondary visual anchor, bridging the space between the subject and the center line.
Horizontal black lines on the right side create a rhythmic, ladder-like structure for the primary text.
Color-coded typography on the right creates a hierarchy of importance among the listed items.
coreInvariants: Hard vertical split at the 50% mark.
A palette of primary red and blue against neutral black and off-white.

compositionAndHierarchy.subjectPositionAndScale: Subject is positioned in the lower-left quadrant, looking toward the viewer, scaled to occupy about 40% of the total frame height.
compositionAndHierarchy.visualAnchor: The subject's face and the metallic texture of the vintage microphone.
compositionAndHierarchy.movementAndEyePath: Starts at the subject's face, moves up to the bold header on the left, then crosses the vertical divide to scan the list from top to bottom.
compositionAndHierarchy.negativeSpace: Heavy black negative space on the left provides contrast for the subject; the off-white right side acts as functional negative space for the text.

colorSystem.dominantColorRole: Off-white and black provide the structural foundation.
colorSystem.contrastColorRole: Bright red and cobalt blue are used for primary typographic emphasis.
colorSystem.accentColorRole: Muted gold/yellow is used for secondary text highlights.
colorSystem.saturationAndValueRelationship: High-value white against low-value black creates a stark, graphic quality, while mid-saturation primary colors guide the eye.

characterSpecificRedesigns: O and C are elongated ovals
S has very short horizontal curves
typographyAndGraphicLanguage.pairingStrategy: Single typeface family used in varying weights, colors, and scales to create internal contrast.

avoid: Centered text on the left side

candidateDirections.reason: Captures the heavy, condensed, mid-century display feel.
Provides a cleaner, more professional 1960s editorial look.

twoStageComposition.backgroundInstruction: Generate a split-screen image. The left half is a dark recording studio with a man in a white shirt and blue tie holding sheet music, standing next to a vintage silver condenser microphone. The right half is a solid off-white/cream panel with thin black horizontal lines spaced evenly in the top half.
twoStageComposition.overlayInstruction: Apply ultra-condensed sans-serif uppercase text. On the left, place a large two-color header in the top corner. On the right, center-align text between the horizontal rules using alternating red, orange, and blue colors, followed by a list of black text below the rules.

verificationChecks: Is the vertical split exactly in the center?
Are all fonts uppercase and ultra-condensed?
Are the horizontal rules on the right perfectly straight?
Is the color palette limited to red, blue, orange, black, and cream?

mustRedesign: Any specific artist names or logos
postGenerationChecks: Check for typographic alignment with horizontal rules.
Ensure the microphone texture is metallic and detailed.
Verify the vertical divider is a sharp edge, not a gradient.
Confirm the subject's shirt is a crisp, high-contrast white.
recipe.reuseFormula: Split-screen [Subject/Environment] + [Structured Typographic Panel] with [Condensed Sans-Serif] and [Primary Color Accents].
